hypothesis: Selecting the frozen E006 interval grid on residuals from an E005-recipe CNO that never trained on the calibration Reynolds groups will either choose a different (alpha, beta) than E006's (0.025, 0.15) or assign that E006 interval an out-of-fold calibration SPS at least 3.0 points below E006's in-sample calibration SPS of 36.250.
comparator: E006 in-sample residual calibration on the same 45-candidate grid and same calibration Reynolds groups

data.normalization: train-only Gaussian statistics over the 45 OOF-training files

training.checkpoint_selection: fixed final update; no validation-based early stopping

interval.selection: maximum OOF-calibration SPS; deterministic candidate-list order breaks exact ties

training_side_calibration.diagnostic_nominal_re: the 10 OOF-training Reynolds groups; recorded only, never used for selection

final_evaluation.source: saved E005 E002-validation point predictions; no new E005 inference
final_evaluation.promotion: evidence only; do not package or submit from E009

controls: E005 checkpoint and saved E002 point predictions remain the deployed point model
OOF CNO uses the E005 recipe except that it trains on the 45 non-calibration E002-training files only
candidate grid and selection rule are identical to E006 and frozen before OOF residual inference
interval selection uses only the 19 calibration-Re trajectories, which the OOF model never trained on
in-sample residuals on the 45 OOF-training files are diagnostic only
E002 validation targets are used once after interval selection
secondary-fold membership is frozen in configs/e009_secondary_fold.json and is not used for E009 selection or scoring
Codabench scores are not used for parameter selection
limitations: One complementary OOF model is not a full k-fold residual estimate.
The OOF model sees 45 rather than 64 files, so its residual scale may differ from E005 even beyond in-sample optimism.
The single E002 split still carries prior selection pressure; E009 does not consume the secondary fold.
Local RTX 5050 timing is not directly comparable with Codabench A800 timing.
